- `width` must be an `int` of at least 1. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- The input is split on Python whitespace, and leading and trailing whitespace is dropped. Words on the same line are separated by a single space.

python3 -c '
import wrap

def check(text, width, expected):
    got = wrap.wrap_text(text, width)
    assert got == expected, repr((text, width, got, expected))

check("  hello   world  ", 11, "hello world")
check("hello world", 5, "hello\nworld")
check("hello world", 6, "hello\nworld")
check("a b c", 3, "a b\nc")
check("a b c", 1, "a\nb\nc")
check("abcdef", 3, "abcdef")
check("", 5, "")
check("   \n\t  ", 5, "")
check("hi  there\nfriend", 8, "hi there\nfriend")
check("too longword here", 8, "too\nlongword\nhere")
check("x y", 1, "x\ny")
check("a bcd", 5, "a bcd")
check("hello, world", 8, "hello,\nworld")
check("one", 10, "one")
check("a\u00a0b\u3000c", 3, "a b\nc")
check("a\u2028b\u2029c\x0b\x0cd", 5, "a b c\nd")
check("hello   ", 5, "hello")
check("supercalifragilistic expialidocious", 1

import wrap

assert wrap.wrap_text("toolong word", 4) == "toolong\nword"
assert wrap.wrap_text("a\u00a0b\tc", 3) == "a b\nc"
